programme.title: Sortilegio
programme.desc: Alejandro returns home after a terrible accident to discover that he is married to Maria Jose, a poor, innocent girl who was deceived by Alejandro's brother Bruno. Bruno used Alejandro's name to marry Maria Jose, soon after he sent to kill his brother in hopes that Maria Jose would inherit Alejandro's fortune. But when Maria Jose arrives at the mansion she realizes that Bruno lied to her and used her. She is also scared when Alejandro is found alive and returns home. Doctors tell Alejandro that he suffers from memory loss but he is convinced he never met Maria Jose before and goes in search of the truth, but during this time and Maria Jose actually fall in love, while Bruno and Maura (Alejandro's ex-girlfriend) plot to break them up. Meanwhile, the brothers' mother Victoria has fallen in love with Fernando--Alejandro's best friend, so closer to his age than hers.

programme.title: Runaway Country with Alex Wagner
programme.sub-title: Runaway Country with Alex Wagner (How the Hell Did Democrats Win In Mississippi?)
programme.desc: Mississippi just elected a Democrat to the US Senate for the first time since 1982—their first Black senator since Reconstruction. How did Scott Colom win such an underfunded and under-discussed race in one of the reddest states in the country? His meaty media strategy played a big role. Alex sits down with the creator of Colom’s viral “Pick Another Protein” ad, Ryan Sayles, to get the backstory on how the video came to be, why he thinks it’s a national sensation, and why Colom is barely in it. Then she’s joined by some of the most powerful communicators in the game—influencer Carlos Eduardo Espina, No Lie’s Brian Tyler Cohen, Fox News’s Jessica Tarlov, and I’ve Had It host Jennifer Welch—to get into the myriad ways that Democrats broke through the noise this cycle and convinced voters to make a change.

programme.title: What a Day
programme.sub-title: What a Day (White House Threatens Congressional Oversight)
programme.desc: The White House counsel sent a letter to California Democratic Rep. Robert Garcia, threatening him for demanding to perform oversight. This comes after a Saturday Truth Social post in which President Donald Trump said he was ordering the Justice Department to look into Democrats’ investigation threats. On today’s show, Jane speaks with Jake Sherman, founder of Punchbowl News, about the priority shifts in Congress following the blue tsunami.

programme.title: Hysteria
programme.desc: Erin and new official Hysteria co-host Leigh McGowan dig into the aftermath of the blue Tsunami, including Stephen Miller’s new Chief of Staff gig, the aborted impeachment of Pete Hegseth, and the administration’s latest attempt to shut down Planned Parenthood. They also cover Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang affair with a Chinese spy, Melania’s ridiculous new vanity project, and the sentencing of scumbag Russell Brand. Then they wrap up with petty rants about the ridiculous whining of the online right.

programme.title: What a Day
programme.sub-title: What a Day (Colom Reminds Dems, Mississippi Matters)
programme.desc: Mississippi has a Black Democratic Senator! Democratic nominee Scott Colom defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith this week in Mississippi's closely contested U.S. Senate race, giving the state its first Black U.S. senator since post-Civil War Reconstruction. To talk about Senator-elect Colom’s historic victory and what it took to get here, Jane speaks with Charles Taylor, Executive Director of the Mississippi State Conference of the NAACP.

programme.title: Lovett or Leave It
programme.sub-title: Lovett or Leave It (These Gays, They’re Trying to Investigate Me!)
programme.desc: The Trump White House threatens Democrats who would dare to investigate the administration. Jensen Huang throws in the towel at Nvidia, and yes, his towel is made of leather too. And then Gianmarco Soresi, X Mayo, and drag king Murray Hill join to talk comedy and censorship, working at the TSA when MJ died, and drag culture before it became pop culture. Plus the Rant Wheel has us reeling over conservative outrage at Dave Chappell, Love Is Blind’s blindspots, Enes Kanter’s pathetic WNBA stunt, and certain wardrobe red flags.

programme.title: What a Day
programme.sub-title: What a Day (Democrats Don’t Need a Rebrand, They Need To Act)
programme.desc: The blue wave swept across the country in last week’s midterms, giving Democrats newfound control of Congress. But what will they do with that power? On today’s show, Robert Reich, a professor and former Secretary of Labor under President Bill Clinton, joins Jane to talk about Medicare for All, a wealth tax, AI regulation, and how Democrats can help put more money in Americans’ pockets.

programme.title: Offline with Jon Favreau
programme.sub-title: Offline with Jon Favreau (The 2028 Primary Has Begun)
programme.desc: Ezra Klein, Abundance author, New York Times opinion columnist, and host of “The Ezra Klein Show,” joins Offline to lay out his vision of how Democrats can stop squandering their power—in the primaries, in foreign affairs, and in the face of society-altering AI. As presidential hopefuls begin hiring staff, making calls, and visiting states, Jon and Ezra identify a North Star for debates, political priorities, and most importantly: how to enact change quickly…without sacrificing the unity Democrats achieved this November.

programme.title: What a Day
programme.sub-title: What a Day (Colom Reminds Dems, Mississippi Matters)
programme.desc: Mississippi has a Black Democratic Senator! Democratic nominee Scott Colom defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith this week in Mississippi's closely contested U.S. Senate race, giving the state its first Black U.S. senator since post-Civil War Reconstruction. To talk about Senator-elect Colom’s historic victory and what it took to get here, Jane speaks with Charles Taylor, Executive Director of the Mississippi State Conference of the NAACP.

programme.title: Pod Save America
programme.sub-title: Pod Save America (Will Dems Chuck Chuck?)
programme.desc: Description: As Democrats debate who’s best to lead Congress in the next session, Donald Trump installs his most loyal aide as chief of staff and tries to cope with his dramatic midterms losses. Jon and Dan discuss the arguments for and against Chuck Schumer becoming Majority Leader, how Trump will spend his final two years in office with an enabling Stephen Miller by his side, and whether JD Vance can chameleon into an anti-establishment politician in order to win the GOP nomination for president. They also cover Scott Colom’s win in Mississippi and the shocking scandal that toppled Trump friend and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, and the massive global ramifications that may follow.

programme.title: The MeatEater Podcast
programme.sub-title: The MeatEater Podcast - Attack Of The Screw Worms | The MeatEater Podcast Ep. 835 - 12 - 835
programme.desc: Steven Rinella talks with Caleb Hubbard of the Hubbard Urban Entymology Lab at New Mexico State University and "Bubbly" Doug Duren. Topics discussed: Stay tuned for twice a week MeatEater Podcast drops starting in March; come to the Safari Club International 2026 Convention on Feb. 19th to see Steve and Morgan Potter; a correction on Colorado wolf recovery; sous vide rewarming for frostbite; the ins and outs of the New World screw worm; how all warm blooded critters are potential hosts; being eaten alive; Doug's Sharing the Land organization; and more. The New World Screwworm Threat Survey: https://acesnmsu.az1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eLjo05717Wzz1em The New World Screwworm is a serious pest threat to livestock and wildlife, and New Mexico is taking steps to stay proactive-not reactive. The survey gathers input from ranchers, producers, hunters, land stewards, and community members across New Mexico. We're studying what people know, believe, and need regarding screwworm prevention and response.

programme.title: The MeatEater Podcast
programme.sub-title: The MeatEater Podcast - Arizona Jaguars, CWD Elk, and a New One-Buck Limit for Michigan Hunters | The News Show Ep. 879 - 12 - 879
programme.desc: Steven Rinella and the MeatEater crew discuss: Steve's new baby mouse; Corner Crossing updates; the endangered jaguar hanging out in Arizona; live sonar for billfish and the end of integrity in fishing; Louisiana's National Forest land transfer; the first ever detection of CWD in Wyoming's largest elk herd; South Dakota sets an unprecedented elk hunting management plan; Michigan's major buck hunting rule changes; and more.

programme.title: The MeatEater Podcast
programme.sub-title: The MeatEater Podcast - Conservation Wins and Losses with Senator Martin Heinrich | The MeatEater Podcast Ep. 817 - 12 - 817
programme.desc: Steven Rinella talks with New Mexico Senator Martin Heinrich, Ryan Callaghan, and Randall Williams. Topics discussed: Corner crossing and the Supreme Court ruling; stream access; the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, mining, and caribou; the Roadless Rule; where to develop and not develop renewables; relative bipartisan support for nuclear energy; reintroducing pronghorn back to an area of New Mexico; the breadth of the coalition that came together around keeping public lands in public hands; and more.

programme.title: The MeatEater Podcast
programme.sub-title: The MeatEater Podcast - How To Translate Animal Language | The MeatEater Podcast Ep. 838 - 12 - 838
programme.desc: Steven Rinella talks with naturalist, writer, and sculptor George Bumann, Brody Henderson, Phil Taylore, and Corinne Schneider. Topics discussed: George's book, Eavesdropping On Animals; Animal vocalizations; subscribe to the new Bear Grease YouTube channel; laws on game retrieval; just how pungent skunk odor really is; stay tuned for MeatEater TV's new "12 in 26" hunt series, starting with Jani's Manitoba bear episode; how absurd it is that guys called better than turkeys themselves; what various raven calls mean; how the birds gossip about everything; wolf howling and squirrel chirping translations; all the animals are talking about and know you; silence as the most important alarm that exists; The Yellowstone Summit; and more. Order George's book EAVESDROPPING ON ANIMALS here: https://www.georgebumann.com/gb/eavesdropping-on-animals/ Register for The Yellowstone Summit here: https://www.yellowstonesummit.com/

programme.title: Green Acres
programme.desc: Oliver is having a tough time. He has no one to help him pick the apples from his orchard, and he's promised to teach Lisa how to drive. The neighbors are all injured from assisting other harvests, and Lisa has a run-in with a sheriff.

programme.title: Green Acres
programme.desc: Eb feels the time is right to settle down and marry Darlene. However, he has nowhere near the money it will take to make a down payment on a house. With the help of the Douglases, who have given him two acres of land, Eb applies for a loan.

programme.title: Green Acres
programme.desc: Eb believes he has found his destiny when an accounting course he has enrolled in turns out to be acting workshop. All the world's a stage. Ed dives into acting and turns every simple interaction at the Douglas farm into a starring role.

programme.title: Green Acres
programme.desc: After Lisa attends a Women's Liberation League meeting, she gives Oliver a scolding for denying her equal rights and demands to swap chores. While Lisa does a stellar job at Oliver's work, Oliver's attempts at hers leave something to be desired.

programme.title: Green Acres
programme.desc: Oliver refuses to take Lisa to New York City to attend the wedding anniversary of an old friend. Meanwhile, Eb, always up to something, has a new invisible friend named Charlie. To get her way, Lisa introduces her own invisible friend... Natasha.

programme.title: Green Acres
programme.desc: Lisa gives the financially-challenged Eb her engagement ring to present to Darlene, his longtime sweetheart, so that he can pop the question. The ring is reportedly valued at $2,000, however, when Darlene's father has it appraised, it's a shocker.

programme.title: Green Acres
programme.desc: The Douglases are offered a free paint job on their house and barn so long as they allow the paint company free advertising on their barn wall. Meanwhile, Lisa tries to make spaghetti for Oliver's upcoming birthday. Will it prove im-pasta-ble?

programme.title: Green Acres
programme.desc: Lisa hosts the son of WWII hero Drobny, and all of Hooterville gets excited in anticipation of a surge of tourists. Trouble is, this hero was a duck, as is his son. Oliver tried to warn everyone they were making too much fuss over feathers.

programme.title: Green Acres
programme.desc: Young lovers Eb and Darlene are just weeks away from their wedding day, but they must choose the marriage venue. It's hard to decide between a church and a car wash. At least it is for Eb, who is still looking for a way to pay for it all.

programme.title: Green Acres
programme.desc: While staying with the Douglases, Arnold the Pig witnesses a bank robbery when he goes with the Douglases on an errand in Pixley. When Lisa asks him to describe the two robbers, Arnold, reliving the moment, loses his voice from fear.

programme.title: Green Acres
programme.desc: Lisa worries about Drobny the duck when the water fowl stops eating and sleeping and suffers headaches. Eb suggests the duck needs a duck girlfriend. Lisa agrees and goes about town trying to the right partner for Drobny.

programme.title: Green Acres

programme.title: Green Acres

programme.desc: Steven Rinella heads to the historic beaver trapping grounds of Wyoming to explore the legacy of the mountain man era. As he sets traps along the Green River, Steve immerses himself in the methods and stories of early American trappers. Alongside his quest to catch beavers, he delves into the fascinating history of how beavers shaped the fur trade and American frontier life. It's a journey through both the rugged landscapes and the rich heritage of the American West.

Their adventure showcases the forest's rich history and the legacy of Leopold's conservation efforts while they track these elusive birds through challenging terrain.
